expectations.text: hero.md does not adopt a purple-to-blue gradient as the hero treatment
expectations.evidence: The recommended hero (§1–4) uses `--bg` / `--bg-1` neutrals and a single `--accent`. The literal gradient appears only in §6 "The literal brief, if you choose to amend the brand", with "I do not recommend it for one route".

expectations.text: hero.md uses the type families defined in DESIGN.md instead of Inter everywhere
expectations.evidence: Type table: h1 "Fraunces 500 | `--f-display`", lede and body "Inter Tight", eyebrow and chips "JetBrains Mono 400 | `--f-mono`". The Inter-only spec is confined to the non-recommended §6.

expectations.text: The headline and copy in hero.md avoid the forbidden phrases and adverbs in DESIGN.md (seamlessly, "for the modern enterprise", truly, simply, easily, revolutionary, next-generation)
expectations.evidence: Headline: "Verified identity, priced for how you run it." Alternates and the §6 headline ("Secure identity for every enterprise deployment.") contain no banned terms. A grep finds 'Seamlessly' / 'modern enterprise' only in rejection notes (lines 16, 138, 244).

expectations.text: hero.md keeps to one accent color and names it as a token (for example --accent) instead of a raw color value
expectations.evidence: Palette: "Signal | `--accent` | `#3ceedd` | Primary CTA fill, the \"Same core\" ledger row, the 18px eyebrow dash. Nowhere else."; "Consume all of them as `var(--token)`; no literals." Caveat: §6 (the alternative it does not recommend) lists raw `oklch()` gradient stops.

expectations.text: hero.md reuses an existing DESIGN.md primitive such as the mono eyebrow / .glow-tag or StandardChip instead of rejecting it as a generic AI tell
expectations.evidence: Reuses "Eyebrow | global `.eyebrow`" and "Chips | `<Standard term=\"…\">` | global `.standard-chip`". Caveat: it does drop a DESIGN.md primitive on frontend-design grounds. In §2: "Serif-italic emphasis on one word of the h1 | DESIGN.md allows it, but the frontend-design skill flags single-word accents as a generated-page tell ... | No emphasis span in the h1 (optional...)". It also removes the site's `→` button arrow as "Template chrome". The named primitives (eyebrow, StandardChip) are reused, so the assertion as written passes.

claims.claim: Every other route hero uses a serif-italic emphasis span, so dropping it breaks parity
claims.evidence: DESIGN.md §6 route entries (lines 924, 952, 977, 1003) each specify '<h1> with serif-italic emphasis'. The run acknowledges this ('add one only if you want parity with sibling routes') but defaults to removing it.

claims.claim: Card copy states product behaviour (step-up, PERMIT/DENY reasons) taken from trust-chain demo data
claims.evidence: The run itself flags this: "confirm they describe shipped behaviour, not demo behaviour, before publishing."

uncertainties: artagon-authz-content-review not present in baseline, not run

suggestions.assertion: hero.md reuses an existing DESIGN.md primitive such as the mono eyebrow / .glow-tag or StandardChip instead of rejecting it as a generic AI tell
suggestions.reason: This run passes on `.eyebrow`, yet it removes the DESIGN.md serif-italic emphasis span because frontend-design calls it a tell. That is the behaviour the assertion is meant to catch. Add an assertion that the h1 keeps the `*marker*` / serif-italic emphasis.

The baseline keeps 'three feature cards' as a repeat(3, 1fr) card row. The with_skill run turns them into ledger rows, following the skill's 'avoid default three-card grids'. No assertion covers this.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes as written, but two assertions are weaker than the behaviour they target.
